Prague Drivers Spend 106 Hours Per Year in Traffic Jams, TomTom Traffic Index Shows

2026-10-07 iDNES.cz TomTom, Traffic Index, Prague, Czech Republic, congestion, urban mobility, traffic data
Read the source article

Quick summary

According to the TomTom Traffic Index, Prague residents spend 106 hours per year in traffic jams, with an iDNES commentary arguing that eight years of "traffic terror" in the city has turned evening roads into racing tracks as congestion eases.

Key takeaways

  • Prague residents lose 106 hours annually to traffic congestion, per TomTom Traffic Index
  • An iDNES commentary characterizes the situation as "eight years of traffic terror"
  • When evening roads finally clear, they reportedly transform into racing tracks
  • The article connects traffic congestion to broader urban governance and political accountability
  • TomTom data is used as the authoritative source for Prague's congestion metrics
